title: Suicide rates highest ever among middle-aged men
titleZh: 中年男性自杀率创历史新高
author: ivewonyoung
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Suicide rates among middle-aged men are higher than ever, new figures have revealed.Men in their early 50s were more likely to die by suicide than anyone else last year, according to data from the Office for National Statistics.There were also increases in suicides among pensioners, with the biggest rise among those aged 75 and older, while the rates among men under 45 fell slightly.Mark Winstanley, the chief executive of Rethink Mental Illness, said the rate of deaths by suicide remained “stubbornly high”.He said: “Every suicide is a devastating tragedy, and these figures are a stark reminder that many people are reaching crisis point without getting the help they need.”The reasons behind suicide were “complex”, he said, but added that many people were “facing significant pressures in their lives, including financial issues, job insecurity, rising housing costs, loneliness and poor mental health”.Suicide rate highest on recordMr Winstanley added: “While these factors affect everyone differently, they can contribute to distress and overwhelm, and leave people at risk of suicide.”The data, which cover England and Wales, showed that 6,162 suicide deaths had been registered in 2025. This was down from 6,190 last year, but the overall rate remained broadly the same at 11.3 deaths per 100,000 people.The stats watchdog uses deaths per 100,000 people to calculate changing rates while accounting for changes in the size of the population.Almost a third of the deaths were among men aged 45 to 64, which was up by 49 compared with 2024. The rate increased to 23.8 per 100,000, up from 23.2 the year before and the highest on record since data collection began in 1981.For men aged 50 to 54 specifically, the rate increased to 28, suggesting this group was at the highest risk.

Men continued to be more than three times as likely to take their own lives as women overall. Among middle-aged women, there were 553 deaths – a rate of seven per 100,000, which was the same as 2024.Sonya Trivedy, the executive director of external engagement at Samaritans, said the figures “show that suicide rates are among the highest recorded rates this century”.She said: “The evidence is clear that successive governments have failed to deliver on their promise to reduce suicide rates and make suicide prevention a priority. Today must act as a wake up call. The current approach is not working; we need meaningful action and proper funding if lives are to be saved.”The data show a growing gap in suicide rates between middle-aged men and those aged 25 to 44.

There were 19.5 deaths per 100,000 men aged 25 to 44 last year, which is the widest gap since 2009, when middle-aged male suicide rates overtook those of younger adults. The rate increased from 14 to 14.4 per 100,000 for those aged 65 to 74 and from 13.2 to 15.4 among those aged 75 or older.Marjorie Wallace, the chief executive of mental health charity Sane, said she was “not surprised” by the data. She said: “Analysis of the contact we receive reflects this – almost 60 per cent of our callers now talk about suicide or self-harm, a very different picture than 10 years ago.“While middle-aged men in their forties and fifties still remain at greatest risk, our other concern is the number of young people, particularly girls and women aged 16 to 24, who report anxiety and depression on a scale not experienced before.”

comments.author: munificent
comments.textRawHtml:
Because it's highly relevant, I'm going to paraphrase a comment I made last week:

I think a big part of the problem is that middle-aged men are at the apex of their expectations to be successful in the eyes of society, and we are living through a period of time where success is very hard to define, much less attain.

There is a name for this in sociology: anomie [1]. Émile Durkheim coined it in his book Suicide, written not too long after the Industrial Revolution.

In times of great change, the set of norms and rules that we take for granted as an organizing principle of our lives get uprooted. It's as if all of the pieces and tokens and rules of the board game we played our whole lives are swept off the table to make room for a new game, but the new game has not been set up yet. In that interim, we all feel a sense of unease. It is our turn to move, but we don't know the rules of the game or what moves to make. We feel intense pressure to play the game well, but don't know how.

In the past, these transitions have ended and society has generally returned to some sense of stability. A new board game gets set up, new pieces doled out, we learn to play the new game. I hope we get to that point with AI soon, but the revolutions seem to keep coming faster and faster.

I think for a lot of men, it feels like just at the time when we should be able to rest on our laurels a bit after having worked so hard to play the game society told us to, the rules have been ripped out from under us and any sense of security going forward is lost. We feel too old to learn the new rules of the game in time to play well, but not old enough to be able to abstain from playing.

It's a psychologically very difficult time.

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomie
comments.textZhHtml:
因为它非常相关，所以我将解释一下我上周发表的评论：

我认为问题的很大一部分在于，在社会眼中，中年男性正处于他们对成功的期望的顶峰，而我们正在经历一个很难定义成功的时期，更不用说实现了。

社会学中有一个名字：失范[1]。埃米尔·涂尔干 (Émile Durkheim) 在工业革命后不久写的《自杀》一书中创造了这个词。

在巨大变革的时代，我们视为理所当然的生活组织原则的一套规范和规则被连根拔起。就好像我们一生玩过的棋盘游戏的所有棋子、令牌和规则都被扫出了桌子，为新游戏腾出空间，但新游戏还没有建立起来。在此期间，我们都感到不安。轮到我们走棋了，但我们不知道游戏规则，也不知道该走什么棋。我们感受到要玩好游戏的巨大压力，但不知道如何去做。

过去，这些转变已经结束，社会总体上恢复了某种稳定感。一个新的棋盘游戏被设置，新的棋子被分发，我们学习玩新游戏。我希望人工智能很快就能达到这一点，但革命似乎会越来越快。

我认为，对于很多人来说，感觉就像是在我们辛辛苦苦玩了社会告诉我们的游戏之后，应该能够在功劳簿上休息一下的时候，规则已经被从我们身上撕下来，任何前进的安全感都消失了。我们觉得自己太老了，无法及时学习新的游戏规则来玩好游戏，但还没有老到能够戒掉游戏。

这是一个心理上非常困难的时期。

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomie

children.author: monknomo
children.textRawHtml:
Well said! 5 years ago I could have a pretty solid picture of what my career would look like through retirement.

Today, unclear what that would look like as well as unclear if the career will even exist that long.

One sunny spot I have is that life is very long. I think I have 1.5 careers left in me, and a full pivot is alright. I've been talking with older folks, and loads of people have historically done giant pivots at midlife.
children.textZhHtml:
说得好！ 5 年前，我可以非常清楚地了解退休后我的职业生涯会是什么样子。

今天，我不清楚那会是什么样子，也不清楚职业生涯是否会存在那么久。

我有一个阳光明媚的地方，那就是生命很长。 我想我还剩下1.5个职业生涯，完全转向就可以了。 我一直在与老年人交谈，历史上有很多人在中年时做过巨大的转变。

children.author: georgemcbay
children.textRawHtml:
> One sunny spot I have is that life is very long.

Not sure exactly where you are in it, but as a 53 year old I disagree. The younger I was the less likely I would have been to disagree but imo/ime the older you get the faster it feels like it is flying by.

> and a full pivot is alright

The AI-related existential dread is that it is very unclear what a pivot looks like when the ground under everything is shifting all at once.

The shifting is certainly a lot more obvious in our career than some others, but all of that shift (so far) happened more or less in a mere 10 months and is accelerating. And I don't think it is very likely that our career will stay anomalous for very long in terms of how much AI impact there is.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我有一个阳光的地方，那就是生命很长。

不确定你到底处于哪个位置，但作为一个 53 岁的人，我不同意。我越年轻，我就越不可能不同意，但在我看来，你年纪越大，感觉就像飞过的速度越快。

>并且一个完整的枢轴是好的

与人工智能相关的存在恐惧是，当一切的基础都在同时发生变化时，我们不清楚枢轴是什么样子。

这种转变在我们的职业生涯中肯定比其他一些人更明显，但所有这些转变（到目前为止）或多或少都发生在仅仅 10 个月，而且还在加速。 而且我认为，就人工智能的影响力而言，我们的职业生涯不太可能长期保持异常状态。

children.author: monknomo
children.textRawHtml:
yeah, you're down to like 3/4 a career left, it makes sense that you feel that way. Less runway ought to feel different.

I do agree that a safe 'next' is unclear. But I also think if ai truly hits all knowledge work as hard as it might we're looking at up to 50% unemployment. Frankly there is no point career planning at all in that scenario. We will all have much larger problems.

And if it doesn't, then pivoting to some field with a combination of rewarding work and 'enough' pay seems sensible enough.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，你的职业生涯只剩下 3/4 了，你有这种感觉是有道理的。 更少的跑道应该感觉不同。

我确实同意安全的“下一个”尚不清楚。 但我也认为，如果人工智能真的像它可能的那样严重影响所有知识工作，我们的失业率将高达 50%。 坦率地说，在这种情况下职业规划根本没有意义。 我们都会遇到更大的问题。

如果没有，那么转向某个领域，将有回报的工作和“足够”的薪水结合起来似乎是明智的。

children.author: spidersenses
children.textRawHtml:
>some field with a combination of rewarding work and 'enough' pay seems sensible enough.

What makes you believe those jobs will still exist or will be available to you competing against massess of other now unemployed software devs? Overabundance of desperate workers will depress wages.
children.textZhHtml:
>一些将有回报的工作和“足够”的工资结合起来的领域似乎足够明智。

是什么让你相信这些工作仍然存在或者可以让你与大量其他现在失业的软件开发人员竞争？绝望的工人过多会压低工资。

children.author: exe34
children.textRawHtml:
> if ai truly hits all knowledge work as hard as it might we're looking at up to 50% unemployment. Frankly there is no point career planning at all in that scenario. We will all have much larger problems.

You missed the happy path.
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果人工智能真的像它可能的那样严重影响所有知识工作，我们的失业率将高达 50%。坦率地说，在这种情况下职业规划根本没有意义。我们都会遇到更大的问题。

你错过了幸福之路。

children.author: rootusrootus
children.textRawHtml:
> yeah, you're down to like 3/4 a career left

If that much. I'm 52, and I wish I had decided 20 years ago that I'd rather do something meaningful. Like become a doctor. It would not necessarily be impossible to pivot to that now, but it would be very expensive and have a good chance of failure. If everything went smoothly, I could be a doctor just in time to retire.
children.textZhHtml:
> 是的，你的职业生涯只剩下 3/4

如果那么多的话。 我今年 52 岁了，我希望 20 年前就决定做一些有意义的事情。 就像成为一名医生一样。 现在不一定不可能转向这一点，但它会非常昂贵并且很有可能失败。 如果一切顺利的话，我可以当一名医生，正好退休。

children.author: bigstrat2003
children.textRawHtml:
> One sunny spot I have is that life is very long. I think I have 1.5 careers left in me, and a full pivot is alright.

I'm 41 and I could, in theory, pivot. But realistically: I'm good at exactly one thing in this world in terms of job ability. I can cook, I can bake, I can play music, but none nearly well enough to actually make a living on it. Thus the end of my tech career, if it should come to pass, basically means I will have to work menial jobs to get by. The future is very bleak for me, and the only real hope is that the tech industry will wake up to what a bad job LLMs do compared to humans. But while I think they will do that eventually, there's no telling how long it will take, and the thought that the market will eventually correct is cold comfort if I can't get a job in the meantime.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我有一个阳光的地方就是生命很长。我认为我还剩下 1.5 个职业生涯，完全转型就可以了。

我已经 41 岁了，理论上我可以转型。但实际上：就工作能力而言，我在这个世界上只擅长一件事。我会做饭、烘焙、演奏音乐，但都不足以真正以此谋生。因此，如果我的技术职业生涯结束的话，基本上意味着我将不得不从事卑微的工作来维持生计。对我来说，未来非常黯淡，唯一真正的希望是科技行业能够意识到法学硕士与人类相比所做的糟糕工作。但是，虽然我认为他们最终会这样做，但不知道这需要多长时间，而且如果我在此期间找不到工作，市场最终会纠正的想法也只是冰冷的安慰。

children.author: vm012
children.textRawHtml: Maybe, in the wake of our primary skill being devalued, we should (try to) combine multiple skills into something that has economic value, as Scott Adams put it - https://web.archive.org/web/20250910155157/https://dilbertbl...
children.textZhHtml: 也许，在我们的主要技能被贬值之后，我们应该（尝试）将多种技能组合成具有经济价值的东西，正如 Scott Adams 所说 - https://web.archive.org/web/20250910155157/https://dilbertbl...

children.author: electriclove
children.textRawHtml:
The LLMs actually do a better job compared to humans.. and it will only continue to improve

I'm in the same boat as you. I'm not sure what the pivot is.
children.textZhHtml:
与人类相比，法学硕士实际上做得更好......而且只会继续改进

我和你处境相同。我不确定枢轴是什么。

children.author: coldtea
children.textRawHtml:
>loads of people have historically done giant pivots at midlife

Lots of people didn't have their field automated away though alongside most other knowledge work fields, or seen at the same time a drop in demand in manual work and an oversupply (drop in demand because of upcoming AI layoffs, and oversupply in manual fields, because of same)
children.textZhHtml:
>历史上有很多人在中年时做过巨大的转变

尽管与大多数其他知识工作领域一样，很多人并没有让他们的领域自动化，或者同时看到体力工作需求下降和供过于求（由于即将到来的人工智能裁员导致需求下降，而手工领域也因此供过于求）

children.author: tempest_
children.textRawHtml:
Everyone can't be a plumber.

In fact one of the worst "trade offs" of the trades is they can very much be a young mans game.

It gets real hard to sling water heaters up/down tight stairs or pull cable in a 100+ degree attic into your 50s.
children.textZhHtml:
不是每个人都能成为水管工。

事实上，该行业最糟糕的“权衡”之一是它们很可能成为年轻人的游戏。

在狭窄的楼梯上吊热水器或在 50 多岁的情况下在 100 多度的阁楼中拉电缆真的很困难。

children.author: darth_avocado
children.textRawHtml:
> Everyone can't be a plumber.

Yes, but not for the reasons you say. It’s because if everyone is a plumber, you don’t need plumbers.
children.textZhHtml:
> 每个人都不可能成为水管工。

是的，但不是出于你所说的原因。因为如果人人都是水管工，就不需要水管工了。

children.author: auyez
children.textRawHtml: Also I imagine a lot of demand for plumbers might drop because AI might help you to learn to solve easy cases. Imagine you turn on you camera and it would just tell you what to do exactly.
children.textZhHtml: 此外，我认为对管道工的大量需求可能会下降，因为人工智能可能会帮助您学习解决简单的情况。想象一下，您打开相机，它只会告诉您具体该怎么做。

children.author: fodkodrasz
children.textRawHtml: I have just called a plumber to do a leaking radiator replacement. Not because I don't have the tools or I don't have YouTube, but because I didn't want to do it.
children.textZhHtml: 我刚刚打电话给水管工来更换泄漏的散热器。不是因为我没有工具或者没有 YouTube，而是因为我不想这样做。

children.author: coldtea
children.textRawHtml:
That was always true if you could afford it.

But get a little more squeezed and with less salary due to AI eliminating your job or your field's salary bargaining power, and you'll try to not call one if you can avoid it, even if you don't want to do it yourself.
children.textZhHtml:
如果你能负担得起的话，这总是正确的。

但是，由于人工智能消除了你的工作或你所在领域的薪资议价能力，你会受到更多的挤压，工资也更少，如果你能避免的话，你会尽量不打电话给别人，即使你不想自己这样做。

children.author: fodkodrasz
children.textRawHtml:
Currently AI made me way more work and unpaid over hours already buy sorting out the 10x expectations and the slop grenades by the 10x workers, that is why i needed it... so I can't even have this much feeling of having accomplished anything myself.

I'm not sure how this will work out. Burnout will be standard, and almost universal soon, apart from the previous low-performer, low skilled bottom of barrel folks who will mass produce crap with this.
children.textZhHtml:
目前，人工智能让我做了更多的工作，而且在几个小时内没有报酬，已经购买了 10 倍的期望和 10 倍工人的残渣手榴弹，这就是我需要它的原因......所以我什至没有自己完成任何事情的感觉。

我不确定这会如何解决。倦怠将成为标准，并且很快就会普遍存在，除了以前表现不佳、技术低下的底层人员，他们会因此大量生产垃圾。

children.author: dranudin
children.textRawHtml:
Yes, buuut: I think we are already really close to that for a long time. You could learn a lot just from internet and youtube. But most people, I feel, just do not like to neither do plumbing/diy nor learn about it. Like if I tell people they can save hundreds of € by changing their own brake pads and that it is really easy to diy, they just shrug and go to the mechanic.
So I am not sure if AI will really increase the percentage of people willing to learn these skills and do repairs etc
children.textZhHtml:
是的，但是：我认为我们已经非常接近这个目标很长一段时间了。你可以从互联网和 YouTube 上学到很多东西。但我觉得，大多数人就是不喜欢做管道/DIY，也不喜欢了解它。就像如果我告诉人们他们可以通过更换自己的刹车片节省数百欧元，而且这很容易DIY，他们只是耸耸肩然后去找机械师。
所以我不确定人工智能是否真的会增加愿意学习这些技能和进行维修等的人的比例

children.author: cucumber3732842
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah the information has been available for awhile. What stops people is all the indoctrination and conditioning.

"I'm not allowed to replace my water heater, the government says I need permits, the government says only a plumber can connect a gas line"

I don't think people realize that the people doing entry level skilled work like replacing your water heater or swapping your brakes at jiffy lube often only exceed the caliber of labor that's in a McDonalds when it comes to attendance and pissing clean.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，该信息已经存在一段时间了。 阻止人们的是所有的灌输和调节。

“我不被允许更换热水器，政府说我需要许可证，政府说只有水管工才能连接煤气管道”

我认为人们没有意识到，那些从事初级技术工作的人，比如更换热水器或在 jiffy lube 更换刹车，在出勤和小便方面往往只超过了麦当劳的劳动力水平干净。

children.author: dd8601fn
children.textRawHtml:
Some stuff you really shouldn’t do just because you saw some youtube videos, and it has fuck-all to do with “government indoctrination.”

I grew up in trades. I’ve seen shit work and dangerous work and serviceable work and beautiful work. And sometimes even I didn’t actually know the difference until an inspector (and family member) explained it.

So I do small stuff. If it’s serious and I can afford it, I use a trusted professional.
children.textZhHtml:
有些事情你真的不应该仅仅因为你看了一些 YouTube 视频就去做，而这完全与“政府灌输”有关。

我是在交易中长大的。我见过糟糕的工作、危险的工作、有用的工作和美丽的工作。有时甚至我自己也不知道其中的区别，直到检查员（和家庭成员）解释为止。

所以我做一些小事情。如果情况严重并且我负担得起，我会聘请值得信赖的专业人士。
